region: Pommard · Côte de Beaune, Burgundy, France
about: Alain Corcia is a Burgundy négociant based in Savigny-lès-Beaune who has spent more than thirty-five years selecting and selling wines from the Côte d’Or and beyond; his Southern Rhône selections are also known to Wine Advocate readers. As a négociant he buys grapes or young wine from growers and finishes, bottles and labels it under his own name. In 2021 the family went a step further: his youngest son Raphaël took over a small domaine in Mercurey, now farmed organically under the name Domaine Alain & Raphaël Corcia.

This bottle comes from Pommard, the Côte de Beaune village famous for some of Burgundy’s most structured, deeply coloured Pinot Noirs. Les Vignots is a village-level vineyard (lieu-dit) set near the top of the hill above the village, a steep, south-facing slope with shallow, pale, limestone-rich soils. Being a village wine named for a single site, it shows the character of one specific parcel rather than a blend from across the commune. At seven or eight years old the 2018, from a warm, ripe vintage, has moved into its mature phase. Expect cherry and black currant with gentle spice, soft tannins and a warm, powerful, complex finish.
facts: Upper slope, south-facing, shallow white limestone soils
